headline: The change adds a simple activity log for each web request, leaves out customer details, and looks safe to ship.
what_changed: Every request to the app now adds one line to the activity log. The line shows the action, the web address used, the result, and how long it took.
Customer details sent with requests, such as Social Security numbers and bank details, are deliberately kept out of this log.
Extra text after the question mark in a web address is also left out.
Staff will be able to see which requests fail and which are slow.
Each request now sends one more message to the outside log service, so the amount sent grows with traffic.

risks.title: Outside log service bill grows with every request
risks.explanation: Each visit to the app now sends one more message to the outside log service (Better Stack). Those services often charge by volume, so costs rise as traffic rises. This is small and expected, but it should be watched. Check the log service's usage and bill after release.

risks.title: Requests that crash may leave no log line
risks.explanation: The new log line is written only after the app finishes a request. If a request crashes with an unhandled error, no line is written, which weakens the goal of seeing which calls fail. This does not affect customers, but failures may be harder to diagnose. Ask the developer whether crashed requests should also be logged.

risks.title: Future web addresses could carry personal data into the logs
risks.explanation: The full web address is logged. The only address today is the loan application page, which carries no customer ID, so no personal data reaches the logs now. If a future address includes a customer's name or ID, that detail would be sent to the outside service and kept for about 30 days. Developers should keep personal details out of web addresses.

questions_for_developer: Can you test whether the existing log-sending setup sends its own internal messages back into itself, which could flood the log service and raise our bill? Please confirm before we add more logging.
Can you make sure requests that crash with an error still get a log line, so we can see failures?
Is our outside log service approved to hold loan-related business names and loan amounts for about 30 days? Can a business name ever be a person's full name?
If we add customer IDs to web addresses later, can we keep them out of the logs?
good_news: The change is small and contained: 29 lines in three files, and it is easy to undo.
The new log line deliberately leaves out request bodies, headers and search text, which is the right privacy choice for loan applications.
The only web address today takes no customer ID, so no personal details reach the new log lines.
